A graduate research university at Thuwal on the Red Sea coast of Saudi Arabia, north of Jeddah, opened in 2009. It was the kingdom's first university where men and women study together.

King Abdullah founded it and gave it one of the largest university endowments in the world. He wanted a place where science could thrive, and he spoke of reviving the learning of Baghdad's House of Wisdom. The state oil company Saudi Aramco built the campus and ran the project, keeping it apart from the religious authorities who controlled the rest of education. Teaching is in English.

Inside its walls the strict rules of the kingdom did not apply. Women did not have to cover their faces and could drive on campus, years before women were allowed to drive across the country in 2018. Some clerics objected, and one was dismissed from a senior post after criticising it.

Most of its students and teachers come from abroad. It works on water, energy, the Red Sea and desert farming, the problems of the region.
sum: A graduate research university at Thuwal on the Red Sea coast of Saudi Arabia, north of Jeddah, opened in 2009. It was the kingdom's first university where men and women study together.
